Name: Chocolatería San Ginés
Tips: 08:00 - Metro L3 Legazpi to Sol. Chocolate con porras at the white-marble counter, open 24h since 1894, and at 08:00 it is empty and magic.

Name: Casa Mira
Tips: 09:15 on the 20-min walk to the Prado - turrón dynasty since 1855, preserved shopfront. Further along, the lions of the Congreso de los Diputados were cast from melted-down cannons of Spain's African wars.

Name: Museo del Prado
Address: Calle de Ruiz de Alarcón 23, 28014 Madrid
Cost Range: 15 EUR/adult, 7.50 EUR students 18-25, under 18 free (~37.50 EUR for four); audio guide 5 EUR
Tips: 10:00, 2.5 HRS, OUT BY 12:30 - PRE-BOOK THE 10:00 SLOT. Do not try to do it; hit the spine: Velázquez Las Meninas (room 12) FIRST at opening, near-private for 10 minutes. Then Goya's Black Paintings (67-68), Goya's 2nd & 3rd of May 1808 (64), Bosch's Garden of Earthly Delights (56A), El Greco (8B-10B) on the way out. Thu hours 10:00-20:00. The free 18:00-20:00 window has its own long queue and 2h is not enough - the paid 10:00 slot is the right call. Timed tickets use the Puerta de los Jerónimos entrance.

Name: CaixaForum Madrid
Cost Range: Free photo stop; inside 6 EUR (under 16 free)
Tips: 12:35, 10 min, PHOTO STOP ONLY TODAY - Herzog & de Meuron's levitating rusted-steel block (they sliced away the old power station's base so the brick mass floats), and across the lane Patrick Blanc's 24 m living wall, 15,000 plants. The British Museum Assyria show runs to Oct 4, 2026 if anyone is still hungry, but the day is full.

Name: Taberna La Bola
Tips: 13:00 - BOOK 13:00, NOT 14:00. CASH ONLY. The temple of cocido madrileño since 1870: each portion simmers all morning in its own clay puchero over oak charcoal, poured out tableside. Served in acts - noodle broth, then chickpeas + vegetables + the meats. 13:00 is early by Madrid standards but it is the first sitting and it is what buys the campus run. SKIP STARTERS, eat the three acts, be out by 14:05. Thu 12:00-20:30, bright-red facade two blocks from the Royal Palace. Book +34 91 547 69 30 or labola.es/reservar. Metro Banco de España L2 to Ópera, 8 min.

Name: Casa Labra
Tips: NO-TABLE BACKUP - since 1860, the bar where the Spanish Socialist Party was founded (plaque inside). Battered-cod tajadas + croquetas standing up, the Madrid pilgrimage snack.

Name: Giuseppe Ricci
Tips: 14:05 on the move, 2 min from La Bola - Roman maestro, dairy-free chocolate sorbet. Eat it walking, do not sit.

Name: Sol Cercanías station
Tips: 14:15 departure - SOL CERCANÍAS IS A SEPARATE STATION UNDER THE METRO. Follow the red-and-white Cercanías signs, not the Metro ones, down to the deep C-3/C-4 platforms. Buy four singles at the machine - THE METRO CARD DOES NOT WORK HERE. 10 min walk down C/ Arenal from La Bola.

Name: Cantoblanco Universidad (UAM)
Tips: THE HARD PIN OF THE DAY: EMILY ON CAMPUS AT 15:00. C-4 from Sol ~20 min, no changes, either branch (C-4a Colmenar Viejo or C-4b Alcobendas) calls here. Station is a ~10 MIN WALK from the faculty buildings and signposting is thin - budget it. Walk her in WITH her at 14:40: the campus is a 1970s grid and she will be doing it alone from next week. Find her building, note the nearest café, agree the pickup plan. Meetup 15:00-18:00. THERE IS NOTHING AT CANTOBLANCO - do not plan to wander nearby.

Name: Museo Reina Sofía
Cost Range: 12 EUR/adult, under 18 and students to 25 free (24 EUR for us)
Tips: 15:50, 1.75 HRS - take the same C-4 back, 15:10 from Cantoblanco to Atocha ~15:35, then a 5-min walk. GUERNICA IS THE REASON: Picasso's 1937 scream at the bombing of a Basque market town, 7.8 m of grey horror, only allowed home to Spain in 1981 after Franco was gone. Stand in front of it 10 full minutes, then find the preparatory sketches in the side rooms. The 90-min route: Guernica + sketches, the Dalís, Miró, the courtyard from the Sabatini balconies. Thu 10:00-21:00, CLOSED TUESDAYS. Entry is free daily 19:00-21:00 but that window is exactly rowboat golden hour - 24 EUR buys the family the lake at sunset instead of a queue.

Name: Centro de Arte Alcobendas
Tips: ALTERNATIVE for the 15:00-18:00 gap if you do not go back into town - strong photography collection, Tue-Sat (verify). Taxi ~10 min, ~12 EUR from campus, or C-4b two stops. Parque de Andalucía's lake is nearby; Moraleja Green / Plaza Norte 2 malls if it is 32 C and everyone wants air conditioning.

Name: Parque del Retiro
Tips: 18:30 - walk 15 min up past Atocha's brick facade to the Puerta del Ángel Caído gate, named for the park's Fallen Angel statue inside, one of the world's only public monuments to Lucifer, standing exactly 666 m above sea level. Into the shaded avenues.

Name: Rowboats on the Estanque
Cost Range: 6 EUR per boat, 45 min (weekday rate; 8 EUR weekends)
Tips: 19:00 - THE BEST FAMILY ACTIVITY IN MADRID, and one boat takes all four. Sun low over the Alfonso XII colonnade, water gone gold, one daughter per oar, terrapins surfacing around the blades. The lake is the 1630s royal pleasure pond where Habsburg kings staged mock naval battles. Ticket kiosk on the WEST QUAY - that is also the meeting point for Emily, ~18:50, off the 18:10 C-4. LAST BOATS ~20:00 - buy the ticket while you wait rather than after she arrives.

Name: Palacio de Cristal
Address: Paseo de República de Cuba 4, 28009 Madrid
Tips: 20:10, a 10-min stroll south through the trees - the 1887 glass-and-iron pavilion, built as a greenhouse for Philippine plants, now a light-box for free contemporary-art installations (Retiro exhibitions run till ~21:00 in summer). Peacocks patrol the gardens nearby; the girls will hear them before they see them.

Name: Puerta de Alcalá
Tips: 20:45 exit - Carlos III's 1778 triumphal gate, floodlit by now. Mirador Cibeles rooftop (3 EUR) is shut by this hour - a daytime option only.

Name: Iglesia de San Pedro el Viejo
Tips: FREE WALK-BY on the way into the crawl - the 14th-century Mudéjar brick tower, possibly the oldest structure in Madrid, leaning over the lane and floodlit. Plaza de la Paja, the city's loveliest medieval square, is one block further.

Name: Bodegas Ricla
Tips: 21:15, CRAWL STOP 1 - KITCHEN CLOSES ~22:00, so this one goes first. Wine from the barrel, boquerones, embutidos in a century-old box of a bar. No bookings, walk in.

Name: Casa Lucio
Tips: CRAWL STOP 2 - BOOK 21:45. Huevos rotos con jamón, the dish kings and Clintons queue for. Closed all August, reopens this week. If the family wants one sit-down instead of a crawl, make it this and skip the rest.

Name: Casa Toni
Tips: CRAWL STOP 3 - oreja a la plancha for whoever is brave, fluorescent-lit and proud. Open past midnight, no bookings.

Name: Casa González
Tips: THE WRECKED-AFTER-THE-BOATS OPTION - family ultramarinos since 1931, 7 min from Reina Sofía. Quiet cheese-and-charcuterie boards, no crawl required.

Name: Cardamomo
Tips: OPTIONAL SWAP - the critics' pick for real-deal flamenco, 100 seats close enough to feel the footwork. Shows 18:00/19:30/21:00/22:30. Doing it means booking the 21:00 show and compressing dinner to pre-show tapas at Casa Toni or Casa Labra. TONIGHT IS THE ONLY SLOT - Sep 4 is Emily's move-in day and ends with the Chamberí farewell dinner.
